title: Modi Is Heading to Three Countries Next Week. In One of Them, Indians Are Being Told They're Not Welcome.
excerpt: The PM's six-day tour covers Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand — where a historic first visit in 40 years collides with anti-Indian immigration crackdowns and planned protests.
body:
India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi will embark on a six-day, three-nation tour from July 6, visiting Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand in rapid succession. The Indian Foreign Ministry confirmed the itinerary on Friday, framing it as a deepening of India's Act East engagement across the Indo-Pacific.

But the trip's most charged stop will be Auckland. No Indian Prime Minister has visited New Zealand in 40 years.

## A Welcome and a Protest

New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon called the visit "historic" and said it reflects the expanding cooperation between the two countries across trade, security, education and technology. India and New Zealand signed a free trade agreement in April that will eliminate tariffs on 95 percent of New Zealand goods and 100 percent of Indian goods once fully implemented.

Yet the visit is overshadowed by a political storm over immigration. New Zealand's Immigration Minister Erica Stanford has circulated draft rules that would tighten visa settings for Indian nationals specifically — restrictions that would not apply to citizens of other FTA partner countries. The proposed changes include a labour market and economic needs test for Indians and a ban on Indian citizens applying for temporary employment visas from within New Zealand.

New Zealand's own Foreign Minister Winston Peters — who opposes the FTA — warned in parliament that the restrictions "target India and India alone" and could damage the country's reputation as a place to do business. His government's own officials cautioned the rules may be open to legal challenge and could provoke retaliatory action from New Delhi.



> **"Meanwhile, self-styled religious leader Brian Tamaki has called for a "Massive Anti-Mass Immigration HAKA" protest at Auckland's Aotea Centre on July 7, timed to Modi's visit."**


Meanwhile, self-styled religious leader Brian Tamaki has called for a "Massive Anti-Mass Immigration HAKA" protest at Auckland's Aotea Centre on July 7, timed to Modi's visit. "If 20,000 Indians can Stand And Take Auckland.. Then 30,000 Kiwis should show to Fight For your Country and Children's Future," he wrote on Facebook. His post included false claims about Christians being unable to practise their faith in India — a country home to at least 25 million Christians where churches, schools and religious organisations operate openly under constitutional protections.

## Indonesia: Critical Minerals and the Malacca Strait


![Prime Minister Narendra Modi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/The_official_portrait_of_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_the_Prime_Minister_of_the_Republic_of_India.jpg)


Indonesia will be Modi's first stop. The largest economy in Southeast Asia and India's biggest trading partner within ASEAN, Indonesia is a major supplier of coal and palm oil to India and holds some of the world's largest reserves of nickel — a key raw material for electric vehicle batteries.

Its strategic location along the Malacca Strait makes it central to India's maritime security interests. The two sides are expected to discuss defence cooperation, maritime connectivity and critical minerals supply chains. Modi is set to meet Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

## Australia: One Million Indians and a Melbourne Event

Australia is the trip's second stop and arguably its most personal for the diaspora. India is one of Australia's largest trading partners, and roughly one million Indian-born residents now make up Australia's largest overseas-born community.

Modi is expected to meet Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, hold meetings with top Australian corporate leaders, and visit the Melbourne Cricket Ground. A major public event with the Indian diaspora is planned for Melbourne, where officials have inspected venues with capacities of 14,000 and 35,000. Australia is a Quad partner alongside India, the US and Japan, and is a significant source of lithium, cobalt and rare earth minerals — resources India increasingly needs for its electric mobility, semiconductor and renewable energy ambitions.

## Diaspora Angle: Why This Trip Matters

For NRIs in all three countries, this tour carries more than diplomatic weight. In Australia, the Indian community has grown rapidly to become the country's largest immigrant group, and the visit will spotlight the depth of those ties. In New Zealand, Indian immigrants are caught between a historic FTA that promises new economic opportunities and a political environment where a government minister describes immigration patterns as a "butter chicken tsunami" and fringe leaders spread misinformation about Indian migrants and crime.

The trip comes on the heels of Modi's visits to Mauritius and Seychelles, a landmark Japan summit with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in New Delhi this week, and a busy June that included France and the G7. The pace of India's diplomatic calendar reflects a deliberate push to diversify partnerships as global supply chains shift and Indo-Pacific competition intensifies.

For the roughly 250,000 Indians in New Zealand, the PM's first visit in four decades is a recognition of a community that has been building quietly for years. Whether the welcome they receive from their own adopted country matches the symbolism of the visit is another question entirely.
